subtopics.title: The Vital Statistics — Birth, Death and Natural Increase

questions.question: Population indicators are expressed per thousand people per year so that:
options: Countries of very different sizes can be compared fairly
Only large countries can be measured

questions.question: Italy's crude death rate is higher than Uganda's mainly because:
options: Italian hospitals are of poor quality
Italy has a large elderly population while Uganda's population is overwhelmingly young

questions.question: South Africa records about 19 births and 9 deaths per thousand per year. Its rate of natural increase is:
options: 10 per thousand, or about 1% a year

questions.question: The word NATURAL in natural increase signals that the measure excludes:

subtopics.title: Fertility, Infant Mortality and Life Expectancy

questions.question: Replacement-level fertility is 2,1 children per woman because:
options: Two children replace the parents, and the extra decimal covers children who do not reach adulthood
Governments set the figure by law

questions.question: Infant mortality is treated as the most revealing single measure of development because:
options: It is the easiest statistic to count
Keeping babies alive requires everything to work at once — safe water, food, vaccines, clinics and educated mothers

questions.question: South Africa's life expectancy fell to around 53 years in the early 2000s and then recovered by more than a decade because:
options: The Aids epidemic struck before treatment was available, and the mass antiretroviral programme then restored the figure

questions.question: The safest way to judge a country's level of development from indicators is to:
options: Argue from two or three indicators in agreement, since any lone number can mislead

questions.question: On a population pyramid, the bars are arranged with:
options: Males left of the central axis, females right, in five-year cohorts, youngest at the base
Females left, males right, oldest at the base
Both sexes in one bar per age group
Ages increasing from left to right

questions.question: Sides that taper sharply inward from cohort to cohort indicate:
options: High mortality — many people lost between age groups

questions.question: A notch — one cohort abruptly shorter than its neighbours — records:
options: A counting error in the census
A past war, epidemic or famine that killed members of that generation or suppressed its births

questions.question: If 30% of a population is under 15 and 6% is over 64, the dependency ratio is about:

subtopics.title: Three Pyramid Shapes and South Africa's Own

questions.question: An expansive pyramid — broad base tapering to a needle peak — is typical of:
Population momentum means that a country with an expansive pyramid:
options: Stops growing the moment fertility falls
Keeps growing for decades because today's giant child cohorts become tomorrow's giant parent cohorts
Shrinks as soon as death rates rise

questions.question: A constrictive pyramid — base narrower than the bars above it — tells you that:
options: The birth rate has just risen sharply
Fertility has fallen below replacement: fewer young children than young adults, an ageing, contracting population
The country has heavy immigration of children

questions.question: South Africa's demographic dividend refers to:
options: An unusually large working-age share relative to dependants — a window that pays off only if the bulge finds work

questions.question: Natural increase, in plain words, is:
options: The speed a population grows on its own — births minus deaths — before migration is counted
The number of babies born each year

questions.question: A country where half of all babies die but survivors reach eighty has a life expectancy around forty. This shows that:
options: Nobody in that country grows old
Life expectancy is an average dragged down hard by infant deaths — a low figure never means no elders

questions.question: The Italy-and-Uganda comparison teaches that before trusting any rate you must ask:
options: Which continent the country is on
WHO makes up the population — its age structure
How large the country's area is

subtopics.title: The Pyramid as a Family Photograph

questions.question: In the photograph picture, a front row SHORTER than the rows behind it means:
options: The photographer ran out of space
The oldest generation is the largest
The nation has slowed its baby-making — births are declining

questions.question: In the back rows of the photograph, the female side usually outnumbers the male side because:
options: More girls are born than boys

questions.question: The three blocks of the crowd used for the dependency question are:
options: Under-15s and over-64s as dependants, with the 15-to-64 middle block earning for all three

subtopics.title: Wide Base, Narrow Base — What the Shape Tells You

questions.question: The column-shaped stack — layers of nearly equal width, narrowing only near the top — represents:
options: The stationary shape of countries like Australia and Denmark, where births balance deaths

questions.question: Rolling a constrictive stack forward thirty years produces:
options: A wider base and faster growth
The bulging middle risen into a heavy top — many pensioners balanced on few workers

questions.question: South Africa's pyramid is best described as:
options: Transitional — between expansive and stationary, with a bulge in the twenties and thirties

questions.question: South Africa's demographic dividend converts into prosperity only if:
options: More people move to the countryside
The economy provides jobs for the outsized working-age bulge
